content.comment_body: Why does [product_name] write the coil register using Modbus protocol to an address one lower than the one specified in the Modbus connection settings? My settings are shown in the attached screenshot. I write to address 1005 and 1006, but [product_name] sends via Modbus protocol: 01 01 00 00 00 06 01 05 03 EC 00 00 (which is for address 1006) and 00 00 00 00 00 06 01 05 03 ED FF 00 (which is for address 1005). Why does this happen? [user_name]
You should direct this question to [company_name] support. Consider starting a support request.

Check the topic, last post from [user_name] dated 9/8/2017 11:41 PM: 'How to read/write [product_name] variables/inputs/outputs and view them on PC software via Modbus TCP Connection?' That user reported the same issue.
Hello. The port configuration seems fine, but the addressing of the coil register in Modbus protocol is incorrect.
In my previous post, I didn't mention anything about the port. I recommended reviewing the linked topic post.

analysis.insight_summary: A user observes that [product_name] writes to coil addresses in Modbus protocol, but the actual address written is consistently one lower than the configured value. This discrepancy leads to confusion regarding how coil address mapping works with Modbus in [product_name]. Other users have reported similar behavior, suggesting uncertainty in how coil addressing is implemented.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the coil address configured in the Modbus settings of [product_name] to exactly match the addresses being written to on the Modbus network.
